subject: CloudMed request: cash-withhold / short-term escrow in lieu of credits
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudmed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudmed.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: CloudMed SLA conversation — ask for escrow / cash-withhold

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to surface one outstanding commercial point before we move to redlines: CloudMed is comfortable with credits for brief outages, but they want a short-term cash-withhold / escrow alternative for repeat severe incidents. High level: a 3-strike P1 in a 30-day rolling window or sustained >50% latency degradation for 5 consecutive business days would trigger a temporary hold of a percentage of monthly fees into escrow (release upon remediation or applied as fee if remediation fails).

We know Redwood's standard position is credits-only; this is a hard ask from our compliance and product risk teams because of our regulatory obligations. Can you confirm whether Redwood will consider a capped cash-withhold mechanism (we suggested 10–20% of MRC) and a termination carveout if the condition isn't resolved within 60 days of trigger?

Attached is a short note from our legal team explaining why credits alone don't meet their audit scope.

Appreciate a quick read — willing to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow.

Best,
Amit

[Attachment: CloudMed_SLA_ask_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Amit —

Thanks for the note and the attachment. Appreciate the context. Short answer: Redwood's public stance is credits as the primary remedy, but for committed contracts we can discuss structured alternatives that limit our cash exposure while addressing your audit team's needs.

A few clarifying questions that will help our legal/finance review:
- Desired cap (percent of monthly committed spend or absolute $).
- Exact trigger definition for "P1" (you included 3 strikes / 30 days; is that aligned with your ops definition?).
- Preferred cure/remediation timeline and whether CloudMed expects automatic termination after the trigger or only after an extended failure to remediate.

Internal next steps: I've looped in Ben (AE) and Neha (Legal). Ben — please surface the committed MRC so we can translate % -> $ for finance. Neha/Marissa — can you weigh in on whether a 60-day termination path is realistic or if we should propose staged cash-withhold + cap + extended cure?

I'm available for a 20–30 min call tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: CloudMed SLA conversation — ask for escrow / cash-withhold

Logan —

Thanks — quick answers below so you have something concrete for legal & finance: 
- Cap: propose 15% of MRC held in escrow (pro-rated monthly) while an incident state is active; if unresolved after the remediation window, Customer may apply escrow to fees or request a one-time cash payment equal to the escrowed amount.
- Triggers: 3 P1 incidents in a 30-day rolling window OR average 95th-percentile tail latency > 2.5x baseline for 5 consecutive business days.
- Cure timeline: Customer requests 60 days from trigger for remediation; if after 60 days the issue persists and materially impacts production, Customer would like the right to terminate for convenience with a waiver of termination fees.

We included a draft DocuSign link for a narrow addendum they can sign to capture the escrow arrangement — aim is to keep this limited in scope and sunset after the initial 12-month term unless renewed.

If Redwood can dispatch a focused counterproposal by next week we'll move forward to redlines. Happy to talk if helpful.

Regards,
Amit

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: CloudMed SLA conversation — ask for escrow / cash-withhold

Looping in a quick internal read. Thoughts below — please treat as internal and not for customer.

On the ask: we should avoid open-ended cash exposure and avoid automatic termination at 60 days. Counterproposal we can take to CloudMed:
- Allow a short-term escrow: cap at 1.0x monthly recurring charge (MRC) in absolute dollars (this maps to ~15% for their hinted MRC; finance to confirm). Escrow is not cumulative month-to-month — it caps at 1.0x MRC.
- Triggers: accept their 3-strike / 30-day P1 rule and the sustained latency metric as an alternative trigger, but require an operational confirmation step (incident review call) before escrow placement.
- Cure timeline: propose staged cure windows — initial 14-day remediation effort (we provide rollback/fix plan), second 30-day operational stabilization period; only if after 90 days the problem remains materially unresolved would termination be considered. This gives us a 90-day total path rather than 60-day.
- Financial remedy: prefer to limit cash to escrow application (i.e., Redwood pays via applying escrow, not additional liquidated damages). If customer insists on a cash payment option, cap it to the escrow amount and require mutual release upon settlement.
- Scheduled maintenance & agreed capacity scaling are explicit carve-outs.

Ben — can you confirm the MRC figure so we can translate the 1.0x cap into $? Also please coordinate with infra to confirm feasibility of the 95th-percentile latency detection window. Marissa — any objections from a legal perspective?

Neha
General Counsel (acting) | Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudmed.com>, procurement@cloudmed.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: CloudMed SLA conversation — ask for escrow / cash-withhold — Redwood counterproposal

Amit / CloudMed team —

Appreciate the specificity. After internal review, Redwood can accept a limited, pro-rated escrow mechanism with the following counterproposal (high level):

1) Cap: escrow limited to 1.0x CloudMed's MRC (absolute cap). Escrow accrues only while a triggering incident state is active and does not stack month-to-month.
2) Triggers: we accept your proposed triggers (3 P1s in 30 days OR sustained tail-latency threshold) but require an incident-review call before escrow funds are moved.
3) Cure path: staged response — initial remediation plan & execution window of 14 days, followed by 30 days of stabilization monitoring. Only if material impact persists after a cumulative 90-day period will Customer be eligible to terminate for cause (we can negotiate the exact termination language in the MSA).
4) Financial remedy: escrow can be applied to outstanding invoices or refunded if resolved. If Customer requests a cash-out instead of application, cash-out is limited to the escrow balance (no additional liquidated damages).
5) Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance (48-hour prior notice), agreed capacity scaling events, and force majeure are excluded.

Next steps: Ben will confirm MRC and provide the dollar mapping. If CloudMed is fine in principle, Neha/Marissa will circulate a short addendum draft for review (DocuSign link to follow). I can also book a 30-minute call to walk through operational implications — pick a slot here: https://calendly.com/logan-wright/30min

If this broadly aligns, we can move straight to a short addendum rather than full contract rework.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
